He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]] and completed his junior season for the [[2016–17 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2016–17 season]]. He was drafted 17th overall in the [[2017 NBA draft]] by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], where he spent four seasons before he was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in March 2021. ==Early life and education== At Capital Christian School in Sacramento, Wilson endured a fifth [[lumbar vertebrae|lumbar vertebra]] [[stress fracture]], which sidelined him during the summer of 2012 and part of his junior season, which caused him to lose the attention of some recruiters. He spent three months in a back brace from his hips to his chest. By the middle of his junior season, he completed a 1-year 5-inch growth spurt that took him to a height of {{convert|6|ft|8|in|m|2}}. By June 2013, he had recovered enough to tally 22 [[point (basketball)|points]] and 8 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] against [[Ivan Rabb]] at a [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California Golden Bears]] camp event at [[Haas Pavilion]]. Soon thereafter, Michigan and other schools began recruiting him. [[2012–13 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|The defending 2013 national runner-up Wolverines]] hosted him (and [[Devin Booker]]) during the first weekend of October 2013 and he accepted Michigan over offers from [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]], and [[Harvard Crimson men's basketball|Harvard]].{{cite web |url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2013/10/michigan_hoops_commit_dj_wilso.html|title=Michigan hoops commit D.J. Wilson took advantage of 'defining moment' in recruitment|access-date=April 5, 2017|date=October 7, 2013 |website=[[MLive.com]]|author=Quinn, Brendan F.}} Wilson signed his [[National Letter of Intent]] with Michigan on November 13, 2013, with the expectation that [[Jordan Morgan (basketball)|Jordan Morgan]] would graduate from the [[2013–14 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2013–14 Wolverines team]] and both [[Glenn Robinson III]] and [[Mitch McGary]] would enter the [[2014 NBA draft]]. At the time of his signing, he was believed to be the first [[Sacramento metropolitan area|Sacramento area]] player to ever sign with a [[Big Ten Conference]] school.{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2013/11/dj_wilson_submits_nli_becomes.html|title=D.J. Wilson submits NLI, becomes second official member of Michigan basketball's 2014 class|access-date=November 17, 2013|date=November 13, 2013|publisher=[[MLive.com]]|author=Quinn, Brendan F.}} Wilson posted 29 points for Capital Christian School against Rabb and [[Bishop O'Dowd High School]] in the Northern California Open Division championship loss on March 22, 2014.{{cite web|url=http://www.sfgate.com/preps/article/O-Dowd-beats-Capital-Christian-70-60-for-NorCal-5341348.php|title=O'Dowd beats Capital Christian 70-60 for NorCal title|access-date=September 21, 2017|date=March 22, 2014|work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|author=Stephens, Mitch}} After having committed to Michigan as the 135th ranked prospect of the national class of 2014 in October 2013, Wilson's ranking rose to 86th by April 2014 according to Rivals.{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2014/04/michgian_signees_kameron_chatm.html|title=Michigan signees Kameron Chatman, D.J. During the fifth game of the season for the [[2014–15 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2014–15 team]] against [[2014–15 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] in the 2014 [[Legends Classic (basketball tournament)|Legends Classic]], Wilson was injured when he was blocked and knocked down on a [[slam dunk]] attempt against [[Dylan Ennis]]. He was sidelined due to a sprained knee and eventually missed the remainder of the season. Ennis later transferred to play at [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]].{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2014/12/michigan_freshman_dj_wilson_to.html|title=Michigan freshman D.J. Wilson lingers 3 years later|access-date=April 4, 2017|date=March 21, 2017|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|author=Snyder, Mark}} ===Sophomore season (2015–2016)=== On December 19, 2015, Michigan defeated [[2015–16 Youngstown State Penguins men's basketball team|Youngstown State]] 105–46 with Wilson contributing 12 points on 5–6 shooting. The 59-point win was the second largest in school history.{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/121915aaa.html|title=Walton Records Triple-Double as U-M Dismantles Youngstown State|access-date=December 20, 2015|date=December 19, 2015|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151220193238/http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/121915aaa.html|archive-date=December 20, 2015|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400830632|title=Michigan overwhelms Youngstown State 105–46|access-date=December 20, 2015|date=December 19, 2015|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2015/12/another_triple-double_second-l.html|title=Another triple-double? Second-largest win ever? Michigan's win vs. Youngstown State worth more|access-date=December 21, 2015|date=December 20, 2015|publisher=[[MLive.com]]|author=Quinn, Brendan F.}} Although Wilson appeared in 26 games for the [[2015–16 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2015–16 Wolverines]], he only played as many as 10 minutes 5 times. Following the 2017 NCAA Tournament, he began to appear in various mock draft projections for the [[2017 NBA draft]]. On April 10, both Wilson and teammate [[Moritz Wagner (basketball)|Moritz Wagner]] declared for the draft, but did not hire agents, which gave them until May 24 to withdraw their names and retain their athletic eligibility to return to Michigan.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/19127532/michigan-forwards-moritz-wagner-dj-wilson-declare-nba-draft|title=Moritz Wagner, D.J. Wilson As COVID Replacement Player|url=https://www.si.com/nba/raptors/.amp/news/toronto-rators-dj-wilson-covid-replacement-players|website=SI.com|date=December 21, 2021|access-date=December 21, 2021}} On December 22, 2021, Wilson signed a 10-day contract with the [[Toronto Raptors]] after the team was granted a hardship exception.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Raptors Complete Three 10-Day Signings|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/12/raptors-complete-three-10-day-signings.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=December 23, 2021|access-date=December 23, 2021}} On January 7, 2022, he signed a second 10-day hardship exception contract.{{cite tweet |user=Raptors |number=1479530719277891587 |date=7 January 2022 |title=OFFICIAL: We've signed D.J. However, he was waived the next day after suffering a season-ending injury. Wilson From Blue|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/magic-acquire-d-j-wilson-from-blue|website=NBA.com|date=February 12, 2023|access-date=February 13, 2023}} However, he didn't play for them. On September 29, he signed with the [[Orlando Magic]],{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Free Agent D.J. Wilson|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-sign-free-agent-d-j-wilson-20230929|website=NBA.com|date=September 29, 2023|access-date=September 29, 2023}} but was waived on October 13.{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Free Agent Miye Oni|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-sign-free-agent-miye-oni-20231013|website=NBA.com|date=October 13, 2023|access-date=October 14, 2023}} On November 2, he joined the [[Osceola Magic]].{{cite web|title=Training Camp Roster Just Dropped|url=https://osceola.gleague.nba.com/news/training-camp-roster-just-dropped|website=NBA.com|date=November 2, 2023|access-date=December 3, 2023}} On March 24, 2024, Wilson signed a 10-day contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|title=Philadelphia 76ers Sign D.J. Wilson to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-dj-wilson-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=March 24, 2024|access-date=March 24, 2024}} On April 4, he returned to Osceola.{{cite tweet|author=Osceola Magic|title=Welcome back DJ!|number=1775913975152067071|user=OsceolaMagic|date=April 4, 2024|access-date=April 5, 2024}} ===Shanghai Sharks (2024–2026)=== On September 6, 2024, Wilson signed with the [[Shanghai Sharks]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].{{cite web|author=上海久事大鲨鱼官方微博|title=9月5日晚间，D.J.威尔逊已经抵达上海和球队汇合，待相关注册材料经CBA公司审核、公示之后，D.J.威尔逊将在新赛季代表上海久事大鲨鱼队出战CBA联赛。热烈欢迎D.J.威尔逊的到来，就像他在视频末尾说的那样，大家赛场见！Let’s Go Sharks🦈 上海大鲨鱼超话#上海久事大鲨鱼# 上海久事大鲨鱼官方微博的微博视频|url=https://weibo.com/1713437511/OvQl1sbtv?pagetype=profilefeed|website=Weibo.com|date=September 6, 2024|access-date=September 8, 2024|language=Chinese}} ===Cangrejeros de Santurce (2026-present)=== On May 17, 2026, Wilson signed a deal to play for [[Bad Bunny]]’s [[Cangrejeros de Santurce (basketball)|Cangrejeros de Santurce]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].
